cohort: The study included 11 women who had undergone bladder augmentation in a pediatric hospital between 1990-2019 and subsequently gave birth in the same hospital district.
finding: Women with bladder augmentation face a high risk of UTIs during pregnancy, justifying prophylactic antibiotics, and a multidisciplinary team should be involved in delivery planning, with elective cesarean section often being the most rational option, though vaginal delivery is possible for selected patients.
mod_finding: Two patients with myelomeningocele successfully delivered vaginally (one multiple times), while a cesarean section was performed in the majority of cases (14 out of 18 deliveries), with some reporting difficulties accessing the uterus and often involving a urologist.
gest_age: 10 term, 3 late-preterm, 1 very preterm delivery (information unavailable for 4 cases)
